content:
This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will officially roll out to all users on Monday, September 14.

Additionally, the company stated that two features originally available in the iOS 27 beta have been removed and will be made available to iPhone users later through a "future software update": the suggested features in Messages, and the automatic password changing feature.

Apple updated its website this week to reflect that the aforementioned features have now been pulled from iOS 27. This change also applies to other platforms, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users had previously noticed that the automatic password changing feature was removed in the fifth beta of iOS 27, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm the change.

As a recap, the suggested features in the Messages app allow you to add relevant items from your conversations to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with a single tap.

Here is Apple's description of the Passwords feature:

The Passwords app will attempt to go directly to websites where you have weak or compromised passwords, and automatically update those passwords for you. At WWDC, Apple explained that the feature uses Apple Intelligence and Safari to "intelligently act as an agent on your behalf."

There are currently no further details on when these two features will return to iOS 27. Apple's website simply states that both features will be released in a "future software update."
